items.stem:
Twelve students each took a spelling test. These are their scores.

7   12   5   9   14   5   11   8   5   10   13   6

parts.t: Write down the mode.
Find the median.
Work out the range.

sols: The mode is the score that occurs most often.
5 appears three times; every other score appears once.
There are 12 scores, so the median is halfway between the 6th and the 7th.

items.stem:
180 students each chose their favourite sport.
The results are shown in the pie chart.

parts.t: Calculate the number of students who chose football.

33 students chose tennis.
Find the value of x.

sols: The whole pie chart, 360°, represents all 180 students.
360 ÷ 180 = 2, so each student is represented by 2°.
the angles of a pie chart add up to 360°
ms:
M1 for 96⁄360 × 180 oe, or for 360 ÷ 180 = 2
A1 cao

items.stem:
A football team played 30 matches. The table shows the number of goals the team scored in each match.

Goals scored01234
Number of matches69843

parts.t: Write down the mode.
Find the median.
Write down the range.

sols: The mode is the number of goals with the highest frequency.
The largest frequency is 9, which belongs to 1 goal.
There are 30 matches, so the median is halfway between the 15th and the 16th value.
The 15th value is 1 and the 16th value is 2.
values 7 to 15 are all 1; values 16 to 23 are all 2
Range = highest − lowest number of goals

items.stem:
Aisha records the number of people in each of 30 cars passing the school gate.

Number of people12345
Number of cars811632

parts.t:
Calculate the mean number of people per car.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

One of the 30 cars is chosen at random.
Find the probability that it contains at least 4 people.
Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.

sols: Multiply each number of people by its frequency and add.
ms:
M1 for Σfx attempted with at least three correct products
M1 for their Σfx ÷ 30
A1 for 2.33 or 2.333…

items.stem:
The table shows the heights, h centimetres, of 40 tomato plants.

Height (h cm)0 < h ≤ 1010 < h ≤ 2020 < h ≤ 3030 < h ≤ 40
Frequency613147

parts.t: Write down the modal class.
Calculate an estimate of the mean height.

sols: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency.
The frequencies are 6, 13, 14 and 7, and the largest is 14.
Use the midpoint of each class as an estimate of every height in it.
This is an estimate because the individual heights within each class are not known.
ms:
M1 for midpoints 5, 15, 25, 35 used
M1 for Σfx ÷ 40 with Σfx from at least three correct products
A1 cao

items.stem:
The mean mass of the 12 boys in a class is 48.5 kg.
The mean mass of the 8 girls in the same class is 44 kg.

parts.t: Calculate the total mass of the 12 boys.
Calculate the mean mass of all 20 students in the class.

sols: Total mass of the boys = 48.5 × 12 = 582 kg
Total mass of the girls = 44 × 8 = 352 kg
Total mass of the class = 582 + 352 = 934 kg
The answer lies between 44 and 48.5 and is closer to 48.5, because there are more boys than girls ✓

items.stem:
80 people took part in a quiz.
The cumulative frequency diagram shows information about the times, in minutes, they took to finish.

parts.t: Use the diagram to find the median time.
Find the lower quartile.
Work out the interquartile range.
Find the number of people who took more than 45 minutes.

sols: There are 80 people, so the median is the 40th value.
Read across from 40 on the cumulative frequency axis to the curve, then down.
The lower quartile is the 20th value.
Reading across from 20 and down to the time axis gives 20.
The upper quartile is the 60th value: reading across from 60 gives 40 minutes.
Interquartile range = upper quartile − lower quartile
Read up from 45 minutes to the curve: the cumulative frequency is 65.
ms:
B1
FT their upper quartile − their lower quartile, with the upper quartile 39 to 41

B1
accept 14 to 16, FT 80 − their reading at 45

items.stem:
96 people were asked how long, t minutes, they spent travelling to work.
The histogram shows the results for three of the four classes.

parts.t: Use the histogram to work out the number of people with 20 < t ≤ 40.

21 people had 40 < t ≤ 70.
Work out the frequency density of this class.

sols: In a histogram, frequency = frequency density × class width.
The bar for 20 < t ≤ 40 has height 1.7 and width 40 − 20 = 20.
the first two bars give 1.5 × 10 = 15 and 2.6 × 10 = 26

items.stem:
Each of the students in a class was asked how many pets they own.
The table shows the results, where y is the number of students who own 2 pets.

Number of pets01234
Number of students46y52

The mean number of pets is 1.75.

parts.t: Find the value of y.
Write down the mode.
Find the median.

sols: The largest frequency is 6, for 1 pet.
There are 20 students, so the median is halfway between the 10th and 11th values.
The 10th value is 1 and the 11th value is 2.
ms:
M1 for Σfx = 2y + 29 oe
M1 for (2y + 29) = 1.75(y + 17) oe
A1 cao

items.stem:
50 runners took part in a race. The table shows the times, t seconds, they took to finish.

Time (t seconds)10 < t ≤ 2020 < t ≤ 3030 < t ≤ 5050 < t ≤ 80
Frequency8171510

parts.t: Calculate an estimate of the mean time.
Explain why your answer to part (a) is an estimate.

Two of the 50 runners are chosen at random.
Find the probability that they both took more than 50 seconds.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: Use the midpoint of each class.
The table only says which class each time is in, not the actual times.
Every time in a class is replaced by the midpoint of that class, so the total 1795 is not the true total.
The individual times are unknown; midpoints are used, so the mean can only be an estimate.
10 of the 50 runners took more than 50 seconds.
The runner is not replaced, so P(second) = <sup>9</sup>⁄<sub>49</sub>
one fewer runner, one fewer of them over 50 s
ms:
M1 for midpoints 15, 25, 40, 65 used
M1 for Σfx ÷ 50 with Σfx from at least three correct products
A1 cao
The actual times are not known / midpoints are used

B1
oe, must refer to the individual values being unknown or to midpoints

M1 for 10⁄50 × 9⁄49 oe
A1 for 0.0367 or 9⁄245, accept 0.036734…
